topics.title: Marine and estuarine habitats and zonation

concepts.title: Estuary definition and geomorphic classification
concepts.description: Define an estuary as a semi-enclosed coastal body of water with a free connection to the sea and measurable dilution by freshwater. Classify by geomorphology: drowned river valley, bar-built, tectonic, and fjord.

concepts.title: Estuarine circulation patterns
concepts.description: Distinguish salt-wedge, partially mixed, well-mixed, and fjord circulation based on stratification and freshwater input. Explain how tidal forcing and river flow control the mixing regime.

concepts.title: Intertidal zonation of rocky shores
concepts.description: Identify spray/supralittoral, upper, middle, lower intertidal, and subtidal zones on rocky shores based on tidal exposure and characteristic organisms (e.g., barnacle line, mussel bed).

concepts.title: Intertidal zonation of sandy beaches
concepts.description: Describe zonation of sandy beaches including beach wrack, swash zone, and distribution of infauna such as sand crabs, polychaetes, and bivalves; contrast exposed vs. sheltered beaches.

concepts.title: Pelagic depth zones (epipelagic to hadal)
concepts.description: Define pelagic zones by depth and light penetration: epipelagic (0-200 m), mesopelagic (200-1000 m), bathypelagic (1000-4000 m), abyssopelagic (4000-6000 m), and hadal (>6000 m).

concepts.title: Benthic zonation (littoral to hadal)
concepts.description: Distinguish benthic zones: supralittoral, littoral (intertidal), sublittoral (continental shelf), bathyal (slope), abyssal (abyssal plain), and hadal (trenches).

concepts.title: Coral reef types and formation
concepts.description: Compare fringing, barrier, and atoll reefs; explain Darwin's subsidence theory and reef zonation (fore reef, reef crest, back reef).

concepts.title: Mangrove habitat and species zonation
concepts.description: Identify mangrove zonation from seaward to landward (red mangrove Rhizophora, black mangrove Avicennia, white mangrove Laguncularia) and associated adaptations to tidal flooding and salinity.

concepts.title: Salt marsh structure and zonation
concepts.description: Describe low marsh (dominated by Spartina alterniflora) and high marsh (Spartina patens, Juncus) zones, tidal creek networks, and the role of flooding frequency in determining plant distribution.

concepts.title: Seagrass meadow ecology and zonation
concepts.description: Identify common seagrass species (eelgrass Zostera marina, turtle grass Thalassia testudinum) and their depth zonation limited by light attenuation; recognize seagrasses as ecosystem engineers that stabilize sediment and provide nursery habitat.

concepts.title: Kelp forest structure and canopy layers
concepts.description: Describe vertical structure of kelp forests: canopy (Macrocystis, Nereocystis), understory, and holdfast; explain environmental requirements (hard substrate, light, nutrient-rich upwelling).

concepts.title: Hydrothermal vent communities and chemosynthesis
concepts.description: Describe vent fauna (giant tube worms Riftia pachyptila, clams, shrimp) that rely on chemosynthetic bacteria oxidizing hydrogen sulfide; explain black smoker fluid chemistry and mineral chimney formation.

concepts.title: Cold seep ecosystems and authigenic carbonate
concepts.description: Explain methane seep communities supported by chemosynthetic symbionts; identify indicator species such as bathymodiolid mussels and vestimentiferan tube worms; describe formation of authigenic carbonate rocks.

concepts.title: Tidal patterns and spring-neap cycles
concepts.description: Differentiate diurnal, semidiurnal, and mixed tidal regimes; explain spring and neap tides in relation to sun-moon alignment; relate tidal range to the vertical extent of intertidal zonation.

concepts.title: Estuarine salinity zones and mixing
concepts.description: Classify estuarine regions by salinity: oligohaline (0-5 ppt), mesohaline (5-18 ppt), polyhaline (18-30 ppt), and euhaline (>30 ppt); describe the longitudinal salinity gradient.

topics.title: Physical and chemical properties of seawater

concepts.title: Seawater salinity: composition and definition
concepts.description: Define salinity as total dissolved solids (g/kg); list major ions (Cl-, Na+, SO4^2-, Mg2+, Ca2+, K+) and state the rule of constant proportions (Marcet's principle).

concepts.title: Salinity measurement techniques
concepts.description: Compare conductivity-based methods (CTD, salinometer), optical refractometer, and chemical titration (Mohr-Knudsen chlorinity) for determining salinity; convert between practical salinity units and chlorinity.

concepts.title: Temperature structure: mixed layer and thermocline
concepts.description: Describe the seasonal thermocline, permanent thermocline, surface mixed layer, and deep isothermal layer; interpret temperature-depth profiles and calculate mixed layer depth.

concepts.title: Halocline and salinity stratification
concepts.description: Define halocline as a rapid vertical change in salinity; explain formation by freshwater input or ice melt, and identify its role in estuarine and ocean stratification.

concepts.title: Density stratification and pycnocline
concepts.description: Explain how temperature and salinity control seawater density (sigma-t); define pycnocline as a density gradient that inhibits vertical mixing; calculate potential density.

concepts.title: Light penetration and euphotic depth
concepts.description: Describe exponential attenuation of light with depth; define euphotic zone as depth where PAR reaches 1% of surface value; relate Secchi disk depth to light attenuation coefficient.

concepts.title: Sound speed in seawater and SOFAR channel
concepts.description: Explain how temperature, salinity, and pressure affect sound speed; identify the SOFAR channel as a depth of minimum sound speed that enables long-range propagation.

concepts.title: Hydrostatic pressure and depth relationship
concepts.description: Calculate hydrostatic pressure increase with depth (approx. 1 atm per 10 m); explain effects on organism physiology and engineering constraints.

concepts.title: Dissolved oxygen and oxygen minimum zone
concepts.description: Describe oxygen solubility dependence on temperature and salinity; explain formation of the oxygen minimum zone (OMZ) by organic matter respiration and limited ventilation at intermediate depths.

concepts.title: Carbonate system: CO2 equilibrium species
concepts.description: Write the equilibrium series CO2(aq) + H2O ↔ H2CO3 ↔ HCO3- + H+ ↔ CO3^2- + 2H+; calculate the relative proportions of bicarbonate and carbonate at typical seawater pH 8.1.

concepts.title: pH, alkalinity, and buffering capacity
concepts.description: Define total alkalinity as acid-neutralizing capacity; explain seawater buffering by the carbonate and borate systems; identify alkalinity as a conservative tracer.

concepts.title: Ocean acidification: CO2 uptake and carbonate saturation
concepts.description: Describe the decrease in pH and carbonate ion concentration due to anthropogenic CO2; explain aragonite and calcite saturation states (Ω) and their thresholds for calcifying organisms.

concepts.title: Nutrient profiles: nitrate, phosphate, silicate
concepts.description: Describe typical vertical profiles of nitrate, phosphate, and silicate (surface depletion, deep enrichment); link to biological uptake in the photic zone and regeneration at depth.

concepts.title: Redfield ratio and nutrient limitation
concepts.description: Apply the Redfield ratio C:N:P 106:16:1 to determine which nutrient limits primary production; state Liebig's Law of the Minimum and recognize nitrogen and phosphorus as common limiting nutrients.

concepts.title: Trace metals and micronutrient limitation
concepts.description: Explain iron limitation in High-Nutrient Low-Chlorophyll (HNLC) regions; describe the role of trace metals (Fe, Zn, Co) as enzyme cofactors and the input of iron via aeolian dust.

concepts.title: T-S diagrams and water mass identification
concepts.description: Interpret temperature-salinity (T-S) diagrams to identify distinct water masses; use density contours (isopycnals) to assess mixing and water mass formation.

concepts.title: Upwelling processes and water properties
concepts.description: Describe wind-driven coastal upwelling via Ekman transport, producing cold, nutrient-rich surface water; identify major upwelling regions and characteristic sea surface temperature anomalies.

topics.title: Marine and estuarine organisms and adaptations

concepts.title: Plankton classification: phyto-, zooplankton, and size spectra
concepts.description: Distinguish phytoplankton, zooplankton, and bacterioplankton; classify by size from femtoplankton (<0.2 µm) to megaplankton (>20 cm) and explain the concept of meroplankton vs. holoplankton.

concepts.title: Diatoms: siliceous frustules and ecological role
concepts.description: Identify diatom cell structure with two-valve silica frustule (centric and pennate forms); explain their importance as primary producers and their role in the silica cycle.

concepts.title: Dinoflagellates: flagella, bioluminescence, and HABs
concepts.description: Describe dinoflagellate traits: two flagella, cellulosic thecal plates, bioluminescence, and role in harmful algal blooms (red tides, paralytic shellfish poisoning).

concepts.title: Coccolithophores: calcareous plates and carbon cycle
concepts.description: Recognize coccolithophores covered by calcium carbonate coccoliths; explain their contribution to the carbonate pump, ocean albedo via blooms (Emiliania huxleyi), and paleoclimate records.

concepts.title: Key zooplankton: copepods and krill
concepts.description: Describe copepod anatomy, life cycle, and role as a major link between phytoplankton and fish; highlight Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba) as a keystone prey for whales, seals, and penguins.

concepts.title: Coral-zooxanthellae symbiosis and bleaching
concepts.description: Explain the mutualistic symbiosis between coral polyps and dinoflagellate algae Symbiodinium; describe how thermal or light stress leads to expulsion of symbionts and coral bleaching.

concepts.title: Mangrove adaptations: aerial roots and salt management
concepts.description: Identify pneumatophores, prop roots, and knee roots; describe salt exclusion at roots, salt excretion via leaf glands, and viviparous seedlings (propagules).

concepts.title: Salt marsh plant adaptations to salinity and anoxia
concepts.description: Describe halophyte traits: aerenchyma for oxygen transport to roots, salt secretion via salt bladders or glands, succulence, and osmoregulation; use Spartina alterniflora and Salicornia as examples.

concepts.title: Seagrass biology: submerged flowering plants
concepts.description: Identify seagrasses as angiosperms with rhizomes, strap-like leaves, and underwater pollination (hydrophily); explain adaptations to soft anoxic sediments and importance as ecosystem engineers.

concepts.title: Osmoregulation in marine and estuarine fish
concepts.description: Compare osmoregulatory strategies: marine teleosts drink seawater and excrete excess ions via chloride cells in gills; euryhaline species (e.g., salmon, bull shark) adjust between freshwater and saltwater environments.

concepts.title: Buoyancy mechanisms in marine organisms
concepts.description: Explain buoyancy adaptations: swim bladder gas regulation in teleost fish, lipid storage in sharks (squalene) and copepods (wax esters), gas-filled floats in siphonophores, and ammonia-rich fluids in squids.

concepts.title: Deep-sea adaptations: bioluminescence and gigantism
concepts.description: Describe deep-sea adaptations including bioluminescence for counterillumination and prey attraction, large sensitive eyes, slow metabolism, deep-sea gigantism, and pressure-resistant enzymes.

concepts.title: Intertidal organism adaptations to desiccation and waves
concepts.description: Identify structural and behavioral adaptations: byssal threads and holdfasts for attachment, closing shells to reduce water loss, hiding in crevices, and physiological tolerance to temperature and salinity extremes.

concepts.title: Marine mammal diving physiology
concepts.description: Explain adaptations for prolonged dives: high myoglobin concentrations in muscle, bradycardia, peripheral vasoconstriction, collapsible lungs, and efficient blood oxygen storage.

concepts.title: Nektonic fish body forms and locomotion
concepts.description: Relate fusiform, laterally compressed, and depressed body shapes to swimming speed and habitat; describe anguilliform, carangiform, and thunniform swimming modes and energy efficiency.

topics.title: Food webs, productivity, and nutrient cycling

concepts.title: Trophic levels and marine food chains
concepts.description: Classify organisms into trophic levels: primary producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, and apex predators; construct simple grazing and detrital food chains.

concepts.title: Primary productivity: GPP, NPP, light-dark bottle method
concepts.description: Define gross primary productivity (GPP) and net primary productivity (NPP); explain measurement using dissolved oxygen changes in light and dark bottles incubated in situ.

concepts.title: Chlorophyll-a as productivity proxy and remote sensing
concepts.description: Use extracted chlorophyll-a concentration as a proxy for phytoplankton biomass; interpret satellite ocean color imagery (SeaWiFS, MODIS) to map surface productivity.

concepts.title: Limiting nutrients and Liebig's Law of the Minimum
concepts.description: Apply Liebig's Law: growth is limited by the nutrient in shortest supply relative to demand; identify nitrogen, phosphorus, and iron as common limiting nutrients in different ocean regions.

concepts.title: Redfield ratio and nutrient stoichiometry
concepts.description: Use the Redfield ratio C:N:P 106:16:1 to assess nutrient limitation; calculate elemental ratios from measured nutrient concentrations and interpret deviations.

concepts.title: Marine nitrogen cycle: fixation, nitrification, denitrification
concepts.description: Describe transformations: nitrogen fixation by cyanobacteria (Trichodesmium), nitrification (NH4+ → NO3-), denitrification and anammox in oxygen-minimum zones.

concepts.title: Marine phosphorus cycle: sources and sinks
concepts.description: Explain phosphate uptake, regeneration from organic matter, and ultimate burial as apatite; identify phosphorus limitation in oligotrophic subtropical gyres.

concepts.title: Silicon cycle and diatom utilization
concepts.description: Describe uptake of dissolved silica by diatoms for frustule construction, regeneration via dissolution of biogenic opal, and silica limitation in the equatorial Pacific.

concepts.title: Microbial loop: bacterial processing of DOM
concepts.description: Explain how bacterioplankton consume dissolved organic matter (DOM), are grazed by nanoflagellates and ciliates, thereby channeling carbon back into the classical food web.

concepts.title: Detrital food web in estuaries
concepts.description: Describe detritus-based pathways: decomposition of vascular plant litter (mangrove, marsh) by microbes and fungi, consumption by detritivores, and the importance of detritus in estuarine energy flow.

concepts.title: Biological pump: carbon export to deep sea
concepts.description: Explain sinking of particulate organic carbon (POC) as marine snow and fecal pellets, the associated drawdown of atmospheric CO2, and the long-term sequestration of carbon in deep waters.

concepts.title: Upwelling systems and high primary productivity
concepts.description: Link coastal upwelling (e.g., Peru, California, Benguela currents) and equatorial upwelling to nutrient supply, elevated chlorophyll, and highly productive fisheries.

concepts.title: Eutrophication and hypoxia in coastal waters
concepts.description: Explain how excess nutrient input drives algal blooms, subsequent microbial decomposition consumes oxygen, and leads to hypoxia (<2 mg/L DO) or anoxia, creating dead zones.

concepts.title: Seasonal phytoplankton bloom dynamics
concepts.description: Explain the critical depth hypothesis (Sverdrup) for the spring bloom initiation; describe the interplay of light, mixing depth, and nutrients that controls bloom timing and succession.

concepts.title: Chemosynthetic food webs at hydrothermal vents
concepts.description: Describe chemosynthetic primary production using reduced compounds (H2S, CH4) by free-living and symbiotic bacteria, supporting unique vent communities in the absence of sunlight.

topics.title: Water monitoring, indicators, and lab analysis

concepts.title: Key water quality parameters for marine/estuarine systems
concepts.description: List the core parameters: temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, pH, turbidity, nutrients (nitrate, phosphate), chlorophyll-a, and fecal coliform; understand their typical ranges and monitoring significance.

concepts.title: Secchi disk and turbidity measurement
concepts.description: Measure water clarity using a Secchi disk; relate Secchi depth to turbidity (NTU) and the light attenuation coefficient; interpret as an indicator of suspended solids and algal biomass.

concepts.title: Dissolved oxygen measurement: Winkler titration and electrode
concepts.description: Describe the Winkler method (manganous sulfate, alkaline iodide, azide modification, thiosulfate titration) and electrochemical/optical DO probes; compare accuracy, detection limit, and field suitability.

concepts.title: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) test
concepts.description: Explain the 5-day BOD test: measure initial DO, incubate in the dark at 20°C for 5 days, then measure final DO; interpret the difference as organic matter load.

concepts.title: Salinity measurement: conductivity, refractometer, chloride titration
concepts.description: Determine salinity using a conductivity meter (PSU scale), handheld refractometer, and Mohr titration for chlorinity with silver nitrate and potassium chromate indicator.

concepts.title: pH measurement: electrode and colorimetric methods
concepts.description: Use a pH meter with glass electrode calibrated with NBS buffers; interpret color changes of indicators (bromothymol blue, phenolphthalein) for approximate pH estimation.

concepts.title: Nitrate analysis by cadmium reduction and spectrophotometry
concepts.description: Reduce nitrate to nitrite with a cadmium column; diazotize with sulfanilamide, couple with N-(1-naphthyl)-ethylenediamine to form an azo dye; measure absorbance at 543 nm.

concepts.title: Phosphate analysis by ascorbic acid method
concepts.description: React orthophosphate with ammonium molybdate and ascorbic acid to form phosphomolybdenum blue; measure absorbance at 880 nm and report as orthophosphate-P.

concepts.title: Chlorophyll-a extraction and fluorometry
concepts.description: Filter water, extract pigments with 90% acetone, measure fluorescence before and after acidification to correct for phaeopigments; calculate chlorophyll-a concentration.

concepts.title: Fecal coliform detection: membrane filtration and MPN
concepts.description: Use membrane filtration with mFC agar at 44.5°C to enumerate fecal coliform colonies; explain the Most Probable Number (MPN) method and interpret results for recreational water quality.

concepts.title: Benthic macroinvertebrate indices for estuarine health
concepts.description: Apply multi-metric indices such as AMBI (AZTI's Marine Biotic Index) or Benthic IBI to assess pollution and habitat quality based on benthic community composition.

concepts.title: Indicator species for estuarine water quality
concepts.description: Identify pollution-tolerant species (e.g., Capitella capitata) and sensitive taxa (e.g., certain amphipods, eelgrass) as biological indicators to infer sediment and water quality.

concepts.title: Water Quality Index (WQI) calculation
concepts.description: Compute a WQI (e.g., NSF WQI) using weighted sub-indices for parameters such as DO, pH, BOD, temperature, and nutrients; interpret the final score to classify water quality.

concepts.title: Sampling techniques: Niskin bottle and depth profiling
concepts.description: Use a Niskin bottle rosette to collect discrete water samples at specific depths; describe CTD profiling, sample preservation (ice, filtration), and field parameter measurement.

concepts.title: Lab quality assurance and quality control
concepts.description: Apply replicates, method blanks, certified standards, calibration curves, and spike recovery tests; calculate precision, accuracy, method detection limit, and control charts.

concepts.title: Nutrient pollution and coastal eutrophication
concepts.description: Explain sources of excess nitrogen and phosphorus (agricultural runoff, sewage) leading to eutrophication symptoms: algal blooms, reduced water clarity, and shifts in ecosystem structure.

concepts.title: Hypoxia and dead zones in coastal waters
concepts.description: Describe formation of seasonal hypoxic zones (<2 mg/L DO) due to nutrient-fueled algal blooms and stratification; analyze the Gulf of Mexico dead zone as a case study.

concepts.title: Oil spill impacts and remediation techniques
concepts.description: Outline physical (booms, skimmers, in-situ burning) and chemical (dispersants) cleanup methods; explain bioremediation using hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria and trade-offs of each approach.

concepts.title: Microplastic pollution: sources and ecological effects
concepts.description: Identify primary (microbeads, fibers) and secondary (fragmented debris) microplastics; describe ingestion by marine organisms, trophic transfer, and vector for adsorbed pollutants (POPs).

concepts.title: Heavy metal pollution: mercury and biomagnification
concepts.description: Explain sources of mercury (coal combustion, artisanal mining), microbial methylation to methylmercury, and its biomagnification in marine food webs leading to human health risks (Minamata disease).

concepts.title: Persistent organic pollutants: DDT, PCBs, dioxins
concepts.description: Describe POPs characteristics: persistence, lipophilicity, long-range transport; illustrate bioaccumulation and impacts (e.g., DDT-induced eggshell thinning in birds, endocrine disruption).

concepts.title: Sewage pollution and pathogen indicators
concepts.description: Discuss sewage contamination assessed by fecal indicator bacteria (fecal coliform, enterococci); link to waterborne disease outbreaks, shellfish bed closures, and beach advisories.

concepts.title: Ocean acidification impacts on calcifying organisms
concepts.description: Explain how reduced carbonate ion concentration and lower aragonite saturation state decrease calcification rates in corals, pteropods, foraminifera, and coralline algae.

concepts.title: Coral bleaching: thermal stress and zooxanthellae expulsion
concepts.description: Describe mechanism: elevated sea surface temperature causes oxidative stress in Symbiodinium, leading to breakdown of symbiosis and loss of pigment; link to mass bleaching events and climate change.

concepts.title: Invasive marine species and ballast water introduction
concepts.description: Identify pathways (ballast water, hull fouling) and high-impact invaders (lionfish Pterois, European green crab Carcinus maenas); describe ecological and economic consequences.

concepts.title: Coastal habitat loss: trawling, development, and sea level rise
concepts.description: Describe destruction of benthic habitat by bottom trawling and dredging, loss of mangroves and seagrasses to coastal urbanization, and wetland drowning due to sea level rise and coastal squeeze.

concepts.title: Overfishing and bycatch
concepts.description: Define maximum sustainable yield (MSY) and overexploitation; discuss bycatch of non-target species (sea turtles, dolphins, sharks) and cascading trophic effects of removing top predators.

concepts.title: Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) and fisheries management
concepts.description: Design MPAs: no-take zones, size, connectivity; evaluate evidence for biodiversity increase, fish stock spillover, and larval export; relate to ecosystem-based management.

concepts.title: Coral reef restoration techniques
concepts.description: Explain coral gardening, microfragmentation, artificial reef deployment, and larval enhancement; discuss genetic diversity and scalability challenges.

concepts.title: Mangrove and seagrass restoration techniques
concepts.description: Describe replanting of mangroves and seagrasses, hydrological restoration to reestablish tidal flow, and use of living shorelines; identify success indicators such as habitat function and erosion control.
